record_type_quote: The present research was designed to conceptually replicate and extend this finding by exploring the effect of workspace disorder on creativity.

targets.authors: Vohs K. D., Redden J. P., Rahinel R.
targets.title: Physical order produces healthy choices, generosity, and conventionality, whereas disorder produces creativity.
targets.evidence_quote: The goal was to conceptually replicate the clutter effect on creativity ( Vohs et al., 2013 ) using another measure of creativity (the Abbreviated Torrance Test for Adults; ATTA; Goff and Torrance, 2002 ) in addition to the AUT.
targets.outcome_quote: Independent-samples t -tests failed to replicate any significant difference in creativity between the Order and Disorder conditions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original disorder effect was not found. The authors report no creativity or executive functioning differences, and explicitly compare the designs and discrepant results to this original.

targets.title: Environmental disorder leads to self-regulatory failure.
targets.evidence_quote: We also compared the effect of experimental conditions only considering the rotations that most closely resembled the task order in Vohs et al. (2013) and Chae and Zhu (2014) .
targets.outcome_quote: Results in our study indicated that working at a messy desk did not result in significantly and reliably different creativity or executive functioning performance.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original disorder effect was not found. The authors report no creativity or executive functioning differences, and explicitly compare the designs and discrepant results to this original.

reasoning: Title, DOI and five authors match. New randomized sample re-tests the creativity effect of Vohs et al. and the executive-control effect of Chae and Zhu. The latter is retained because the study tests the same disorder-to-control relationship, directly compares its results and methods to that paper, and conducts analyses aligned to its task order. Other creativity and executive-control papers motivate mechanisms or provide tasks and are not re-tested. Original study numbers are not specified.
